gap: No evidence of a stable cross-feature user identifier or unified event schema in any public source.
impact_on_future_reporting: Cannot reconstruct a user lifecycle across ads, wallet, withdrawals, and referrals; every cross-feature KPI is at risk.
reason_for_priority: Without one stable user_id semantics, no reliable user-level analysis is possible at all — it is the join key for the entire model (brief example: stable transaction/user IDs).
evidence: SRC-002 (routes exist per feature; no identifier documented)
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed user_id requirement recorded in DCM-035; to be specified in Deliverable 04/08 and verified by Engineering (ASM-008).

gap: Reward lifecycle stages (activity occurred → validation → reward credited) are not defined in any public source, although the platform's own FAQ distinguishes task validation, ad tracking delays, and invalid completion.
impact_on_future_reporting: Gross activity and net credited rewards cannot be separated; completion-rate and credit-rate KPIs would be ambiguous.
reason_for_priority: The brief explicitly requires distinguishing 'activity occurred' from 'reward actually credited'; public docs prove both exist conceptually but define no states, timestamps, or events.
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed reward-state model recorded in DCM-030/DCM-031; to be finalized in Deliverable 05 and event catalogue (08).

gap: No transaction-ledger specification for the six virtual currencies (VEs, XP, Gems, Tokens, Spins, badges); exchange rules, rates, limits, and pairings are public in principle but not itemized and may change.
impact_on_future_reporting: Wallet balances cannot be reconciled to transactions; exchange volume and rate-sensitivity KPIs are undefinable.
reason_for_priority: A rewards platform without a documented ledger model cannot support reliable wallet or reward KPIs; public policy says rates and pairings may change.
evidence: SRC-005; SRC-007 (FAQ: Gems Exchange / Swap Center)
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed ledger fields and exchange events in DCM-020; full transaction model to be built in Deliverable 06.

gap: Reward reversal/correction is acknowledged (system correction rights; withdrawal reversals; reward cancellation on fraud) but is not represented anywhere as a defined, auditable event or state.
impact_on_future_reporting: Net reward and net balance KPIs are unreliable; gross-vs-net exposure is invisible to management.
reason_for_priority: Reversal is a first-class concept in the public policy text yet has no event, reason code, or timestamp definition — the largest silent distortion risk in reward reporting.
evidence: SRC-004; SRC-006; SRC-007 (FAQ: wallet correction; fraud cancellation)
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed reward_corrected / reward_reversed events in DCM-031; reversal relationship modeling required in Deliverable 06 and KPI catalogue (11).

gap: Withdrawal status taxonomy is not published: policy describes outcomes qualitatively (delayed, rejected, reversed, pending review) with no status enum, reason categories, or transition rules.
impact_on_future_reporting: Withdrawal funnel, completion rate, processing time, and pending-queue KPIs cannot be standardized or audited.
reason_for_priority: The brief's withdrawal KPI list (requests, completed, pending, rejected, processing time, completion rate) all depend on a stable status vocabulary that does not exist publicly.
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed status taxonomy and lifecycle recorded in DCM-023; marked Proposed per C2-style rule (no invented internal codes); to be confirmed with Product.

gap: Referral lifecycle stages (created → registered → activated → converted) are undefined; public FAQ states only that 'only valid referrals accepted by the platform may qualify' under fixed reward logic.
impact_on_future_reporting: Referral funnel conversion, quality, and ROI are unmeasurable; registration cannot be assumed equal to conversion.
reason_for_priority: The brief explicitly warns registration must not automatically equal referral conversion; public docs do not even define 'accepted' as a stage with a timestamp.
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed referral lifecycle stages in DCM-024; activation/conversion definitions to be proposed in Deliverable 07.

gap: No session identifier or session definition appears in any public source.
impact_on_future_reporting: Session-level engagement (depth, journeys, feature order) is unmeasurable; DAU-style definitions remain ambiguous.
reason_for_priority: Session-level analysis is a standard requirement (brief: session identifier where appropriate), and nothing public supports it today.
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed session_id and session events in DCM-034; to be decided in Deliverable 04 (identity requirements).

gap: Third-party dependencies (rewarded ads, offerwall, surveys, follow-and-earn, external promotions) are acknowledged with explicit 'tracking limitations' in the public Advertising & Offerwall Policy, but no external validation contract or failure taxonomy is documented.
impact_on_future_reporting: External validation failures, delays, and attribution loss are invisible; completion-rate KPIs would silently mix VELOOP failures with third-party failures.
reason_for_priority: The brief requires not designing analytics as if VELOOP controls every external outcome; the public policy confirms external outcomes are outside full control.
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed provider/failure_type properties in DCM-005/DCM-014/DCM-029; dependency section required in Deliverable 05 (C4).

gap: Payout method contradiction across public sources: home meta says 'PayPal or Paytm'; the Payout UI lists UPI/Amazon Pay/Google Play with PayPal 'Coming Soon' and no Paytm; the Vercel marketing page shows UPI/Amazon/Google Pay/PayPal.
impact_on_future_reporting: Method-distribution KPIs and dashboard filters have no single source of truth; reporting could misstate supported methods.
reason_for_priority: A core withdrawal dimension is inconsistent across the company's own public surfaces; building KPIs on the wrong dimension set would corrupt all withdrawal reporting.
mitigation_in_this_project: Contradiction documented in Deliverable 02 §8.1 and ASM-003; method dimension frozen as 'To Be Verified' until Product confirms.

gap: Registration has no documented acquisition-source, channel, or device fields in any public source.
impact_on_future_reporting: Acquisition source analysis, channel ROI, and device mix are impossible; the registration KPI set would lack its standard dimensions.
reason_for_priority: Registration is a required KPI area in the brief; without source/device dimensions the user KPI group is analytically thin but the core count still works.
mitigation_in_this_project: Proposed acquisition_channel/device properties in DCM-033; to be specified in Deliverable 04.

gap: The product disclaimer reserves the right to change rewards, exchanges, withdrawals, rankings, and offers at any time, but no analytics change-management mechanism (event versioning, KPI version log) exists publicly.
impact_on_future_reporting: When mechanics change, historical metric definitions break silently and trend lines become non-comparable.
reason_for_priority: This is a developing product with explicitly unstable mechanics; without versioning, every retrospective analysis risks mixing incompatible definitions.
mitigation_in_this_project: Change log requirement recorded in DCM-036; full change-management design scheduled for Deliverable 17/21 (Work Package Q).

gap: Public source reliability issues: one FAQ block contains boilerplate statements inconsistent with the product model (points transfers, PCI-DSS/SOC 2 claims, card tokenization); and all evidence comes from a single domain's client-side bundle with individual pages not independently rendered.
impact_on_future_reporting: Any deliverable that accidentally reuses boilerplate would contain false product claims; single-source concentration limits confidence in feature completeness.
reason_for_priority: Integrity rules prohibit repeating unverified claims; this gap is about the source, not the product, but it must be managed explicitly.
evidence: SRC-002 limitation notes; SRC-007; ASM-004; ASM-005
mitigation_in_this_project: Boilerplate excluded from all claims (ASM-004); source limitations recorded per-row in the Source Register; re-verification before each later stage.
